infovore-219-spec:
- Output is a header line whose whitespace-separated tokens are `channel labelled relevant irrelevant %irrelevant exchanges excluded`, then one whitespace-separated row per channel in that order.
- The channel name prints bare, with no leading `#`. labelled is relevant + irrelevant (bad_grouping not counted); exchanges is every exchange in that channel, labelled or not; % irrelevant prints with one decimal and a `%` sign, e.g. `33.3%`, `100.0%`; the excluded column is `yes` or `no`.
- A thread gets its own row and is not rolled into its parent channel. A row is excluded (per INFOVORE_EXCLUDE_CHANNELS) when its own name or its parent channel's name is denylisted.
- When no channel reaches --min-labels, print exactly `no channels with at least N labels` (N the --min-labels value) and exit OK.
infovore-250-spec:
- `threshold_stats` returns `{"irrelevant": {"n", "precision", "recall"}, "relevant": {"n", "precision", "recall"}}`. The irrelevant side covers samples with score < t_irrelevant: precision is the share of them not relevant, recall is that count over all non-relevant samples. The relevant side covers samples with score >= t_relevant: precision is the share relevant, recall is that count over all relevant samples. Any zero denominator gives 0.0.
- The fitted recipe stores that dict under a top-level `recipe["cv"]` key, and `recipe["thresholds"]["relevant_precision_target"]` holds the precision target actually used (default 0.90).
- `relevance cascade` prints one line per side beginning `cv irrelevant: n=` and `cv relevant: n=`, each followed by `precision=` and `recall=` values.
infovore-252-spec:
- The stage name is `short_no_tech`. It goes in the STAGES tuple in infovore/db/archived.py between `lexicon` and `embed`, so its scorer is `relevance_short_no_tech` and stage_reports returns it in that position. Its outcomes count as ruled out, like denylist and no_text. Its decision is `irrelevant`, and write_outcomes stores `short_limit` in that annotation's recipe_json.
- An exchange takes this stage when short_limit is not None, the lexicon did not decide it, it has zero word-list hits, and its text length (sum of each message's stripped content length) is < short_limit. When short_limit is None the stage is off.
- `Row` is a NamedTuple `(exchange_id, chars, hits)`.
- `bucket_of` returns one of `<100`, `100-200`, `200-500`, `500-1000`, `1000+` (lower edges inclusive).
- `bucket_table` returns one line for every bucket x tech (tech = hits > 0) pair, 10 in all, including empty ones. Each line has fields `bucket`, `tech`, `corpus`, `relevant`, `irrelevant` (build labels only), `held_relevant`, `held_irrelevant`, plus a property `percent_irrelevant` = 100 * irrelevant / (relevant + irrelevant), or None when nothing is labelled.
- `best_cutoff` uses only zero-hit, labelled, non-held-out rows. `Cutoff.limit` is exclusive (chars < limit). It returns the largest limit whose rows below it number at least `minimum` and reach `precision` irrelevant, or None. `PRECISION` is 0.95 and `MIN_LABELLED` is 20.
- `cutoff_line` returns `cutoff L=<limit> precision=<3 decimals> n=<n>\n`, e.g. `cutoff L=120 precision=0.970 n=33\n`, and for None a line containing `no cutoff qualifies`.
- `relevance short-report` prints the table with tech column values `tech words` / `no tech words`, the bucket labels, and the cutoff_line.
- `relevance cascade` calls `short_limit` through its name imported into relevance_command, and prints `short_no_tech limit=<n>` when it is set.
- `infovore status` prints `irrelevant: N (denylist a, short no tech b, embed c)`, with N the sum of the three.
infovore-256-spec:
- The `labels` command is a new Command registered in builtin_commands, with `configure(parser)` and `async run(context, args)`; `export` is its subcommand. It writes one JSON object per line to the --jsonl path, creating parent directories as needed.
- Field values: `label` is `relevant` or `irrelevant`. `text` is the llm-score render's lines joined with `\n`. `channel` is the parent channel's name for a thread, otherwise the channel's own name. `slice` is the alphabetically first current slice the exchange belongs to, or null. `cascade_stage` is the stage name (e.g. `lexicon`, `embed`, `short_no_tech`) of the latest relevance_* annotation with a non-null label, or null. `label_source` comes from the latest human_exchange annotation's source_ref: the second `:` part for `judge:<x>:<n>`, otherwise the part before the first `:`, and null when there is no ref.
- Printed counts: `labels: N`, then one line per value as `<field> <value>: <count>` for label, held_out and cascade_stage, with values lowercased and null printed as `none` (e.g. `held_out true: 2`, `cascade_stage none: 2`).
infovore-338-spec:
- Existing repo pieces not in context: `infovore.triage.embed` has `Embedder` (method `embed(texts: list[str]) -> list of vectors`), `EMBED_BATCH`, `DEFAULT_MODEL` and `DEFAULT_REVISION`; `infovore.triage.embed_backend.load_embedder(model_id, revision)` loads the real one. groups.py imports `load_embedder` into its own namespace, and the embed path calls it through that name.
- `ClaimGroup.speakers`, `exchanges`, `span` and `corroboration` are properties. span is (earliest date, latest date) and corroboration is the number of distinct speakers.
- group_claims orders groups by corroboration desc, then distinct exchanges desc, then member count desc, then lead date, then lead claim_id.
- With `vectors`, a claim joins the first group whose lead's vector has cosine >= vector_threshold (`VECTOR_THRESHOLD` 0.85) instead of using tokens. If the vector count differs from the claim count it raises ValueError containing `one vector per claim`. `cosine` returns 0.0 when either vector is all zeros.
- `make_grouper` embeds every claim once up front, in chunks of EMBED_BATCH statements, and returns a callable that groups any subset of those claims by their stored vectors. `make_grouper_for("jaccard", ...)` returns `group_claims` itself; `"embed"` uses `load_embedder(DEFAULT_MODEL, DEFAULT_REVISION)`.
- `summarise` returns an object with `groups`, `by_speakers` (keys `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3+"`), `corroborated_claims` (members of groups with 2+ speakers), `claims` (all members) and a `share` property (0.0 when there are no claims). Its str is e.g. `groups 3 (1 speaker(s) 1, 2 speaker(s) 1, 3+ speaker(s) 1); claims in 2+ speaker groups 5/6 (83.3%)`.
- `--grouping` takes `jaccard` (default) or `embed` on `wiki build`, `wiki stats` and `wiki write`. Both build and stats print `corroboration: <that summary>` over the groups of every page that is built.
- Each fallback page entry keeps its current text but ends `; N speaker(s), M conversation(s))` in place of the closing `)`, e.g. `- Indigo2 has an R4400 cpu (+1 similar) (user-1, exchange 11, 2026-02-01; 2 speaker(s), 2 conversation(s))`, on every entry including singletons.
infovore-352-spec:
- canonical() also strips the en dash and em dash (`N–brick` gives `nbrick`) and backticks along with the other quotes.
- The plural rule applies only to a spelling of at least 3 characters, so `as` never folds onto `a`. It tries dropping the final `s`, and also `ies` to `y` and dropping `es`.
- The generic nouns are machine, system, computer and workstation, singular or plural.
- merge_map resolves chains to their final target (`Indys systems` to `indy`) and stops when it meets a cycle.
- `Merged(keys, tags)` counts the folded keys and the claim-tags on them. Its str is `N keys, M claim-tags`, and `wiki stats` with a tag run prints the line `merged: N keys, M claim-tags`.
infovore-353-spec:
- `claims novelty` and `claim_novelty` already exist. This task is the wiki use step, and the floor flag is `--background C` on `wiki build`, `wiki stats` and `wiki write`, in place of `--novelty-floor`.
- `WikiClaim.novelty` holds the claim's stored reference max cosine as-is (not 1 minus it), and `reference` holds its reference title. Both are filled only when load_claims gets a background value; claims without a row keep None.
- `established(claim, background)` is true when background is not None, novelty is not None, and novelty >= background.
- Within a corroboration level, groups sort by the lead's novelty ascending, with None counted as 0.0, ahead of the existing keys.
- render_page with background moves established claims out of the sections into a `## Background` heading after them. Each entry reads `- <statement> ([<title>](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/<title with spaces as _, URL-quoted>), cosine 0.93; <speaker>, <date>)`, with the bare word `reference` in place of the link when there is no title.
- `wiki stats` always prints `background: N` (established claims), followed by ` (cosine >= C)` when --background is given. `wiki write` drops established claims from its input.
infovore-373-spec:
- corrections.toml entries are `[[claim]]` tables with `exchange`, `statement`, and `drop = true` or `replace`. The shipped file has no active entry. `load_corrections(None)` reads the corrections.toml beside the module. - A statement's whitespace is collapsed (`" ".join(s.split())`), and `key` is a property `(exchange, statement)`. - load_corrections raises ValueError with `correction` in the message when an entry has neither drop = true nor replace, has both, or repeats a key. - `Excluded` gains `unmatched`: a tuple of the Correction objects that matched no claim, sorted by key, defaulting to `()`. - A claim matched by a drop counts as `corrected` only when it has no other exclusion reason. An entry that matches a claim excluded for another reason still counts as matched. - `wiki stats` and `wiki build` always print `corrections unmatched: N`, including when N is 0. - Every build writes `fix.md` beginning `# Fix a mistake `, and `fix` is a reserved file name, so a topic named Fix gets `fix-2.md`. - The HTML nav reads `... All topics | Fix a mistake | Guestbook ]`, and the footer contains `Spotted a mistake? Fix it.` - html `body()` renders consecutive lines indented four spaces (outside a list) as one `
` block: the indent is removed, the lines are joined with `
`, and the text is HTML-escaped without quote escaping. A preceding paragraph is closed first. E.g. `Add this:
    [[claim]]
    x = ""

Text
    more
## H
` gives `
Add this:


[[claim]]
x = "<b>"


Text


more


H

`.

mcm-engine-145-spec:
- `_build_arguments` returns the `save_snapshot` keyword arguments: key "progress" is a text that contains the trigger (an empty trigger becomes "auto"); key "open_questions" holds the custom instructions and is present only when they are non-empty.
- `main` reads `trigger` and `custom_instructions` from the stdin event. When `_mcp_http_endpoint(cwd)` returns a URL it calls `mcp_http_call_tool(url, "save_snapshot", args, headers=..., timeout=...)` and never calls `_write_local`; when the URL is None it calls `_write_local(cwd, args)`. It returns 0 always, including on invalid stdin JSON and when the write raises.

mcm-engine-157-spec:
- `coverage.record_topic` stores `entry["covered_topics"][topic] = now` (a float), the topic lowercased and stripped; an empty or blank topic is a no-op. `is_covered` matches the topic case-insensitively, is False when `now - recorded > ttl`, and with `require_resident=True` is False when `note_compaction` has stamped a boundary on the entry and the topic was recorded at or before it (no boundary means resident). `prune_topics` deletes topics older than `ttl` and does nothing when `covered_topics` is absent.
- `classify` returns `(False, "")` for a non-historical prompt and `(True, keyword)` for a historical one, where keyword is `_pick_keyword(prompt)`. History signals match on word boundaries ("distill" does not match "still").
- `_pick_keyword` returns one lowercased token: the longest identifier-shaped word (contains "_", a digit, or an interior capital) if any, else the longest word of 4+ letters that is not a stopword; history signal words such as "again" are stopwords. It returns "" when nothing qualifies.
- `main` calls `search(keyword, cwd)` only for a historical prompt with a non-empty keyword. A non-empty result prints `{"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "UserPromptSubmit", "additionalContext": ...}}` where the context contains the keyword and the result; an empty result or a raising search prints nothing. Exit code is always 0.
- Coverage is recorded even when the search returns empty: in the existing hook state file of `mcm_engine.hooks.mcp_enforcement` (path from `_state_path(cwd)`, read with `_read_state(path)`, written with `_write_state(path, state)`), under the key `_agent_key(event)` (the event's session_id), by calling `coverage.record_topic` on that entry dict.

- In summary mode each inline NEGATIVE Why/Fix and ERROR Root cause/Fix field longer than 320 characters is cut to 320 and followed by "… (get_entry('negative', <id>) for full)" or "… (get_entry('error', <id>) for full)". detail="full" output carries no such pointer.

mcm-engine-199-spec:
- `ReplayQuery` gains `recorded_bytes: int = -1`: the UTF-8 byte length of the tool_result paired by tool_use id (its string content, or the joined "text" of its text blocks); -1 when the transcript holds no result for it.
- `wire_bytes(text)` is the UTF-8 byte length of the compact JSON `{"result": text}` (separators "," and ":", non-ASCII not escaped).
- `kind_bytes(text)` walks the lines: a line starting "[KNOWLEDGE", "[NEGATIVE", "[ERROR" or "[RULE" opens a block of that kind (key lowercased), a line starting "(", "---" or "===" opens an "other" block, and every other line (blank, indented or not) stays with the current block; lines before any hit count as "other". Each line adds its UTF-8 length plus 1. Only kinds seen appear as keys.
- `ReplayReport` gains `sizes: dict` keyed by tool ("search", "report_error"). `sizes[tool]["legacy"]` and `["unified"]` hold "n", "total", "median", "p90" over the wire_bytes of every replayed result plus "by_kind" (summed kind_bytes). `sizes[tool]["recorded"]` holds `{"n", "total", "median", "p90"}` over paired queries only, median and p90 as floats. `legacy_ratio` and `unified_ratio` are that side's wire_bytes summed over the paired queries divided by the recorded total.
- `format_report` prints a "bytes/<tool>:" line per tool, and each ratio with the text "of recorded".
mcm-engine-22-symptom:

- Each active rule is written to `<out_dir>/rules/<category>/<slug>.md`, slug from `mcm_engine.tools.rules._slugify(title)`, body from `mcm_engine.tools.rules._generate_rule_content(title, keywords, category, content)` (it starts "# <title>" and has "**Keywords:** <keywords>"). A rule no longer active must have no file after the next run.
- It returns `{"written": <number of active rules written>, "committed": <bool>}`; `committed` is False when the run changed nothing.

mcm-engine-25-spec:
- The weights are module constants in `mcm_engine.scoring`: `W_RELEVANCE` (multiplying `normalize_relevance(raw_rank, query_terms)`), `W_HIT`, `W_REINFORCEMENT`, `W_CORRECTNESS` and `W_RECENCY`, with `PINNED_WEIGHT` kept as the flat pinned boost. `W_RELEVANCE` must exceed the sum of the other four (values 2.0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.3), so a strong match with no hits, reinforcement or outcomes outranks a weak match with maximal hits, reinforcement, correctness and recency.
- The saturated reinforcement term adds less than `W_REINFORCEMENT` (0.3) at any count.
- `compose_rank_pinned_only` returns `W_RELEVANCE * normalize_relevance(raw_rank, query_terms)`, plus `PINNED_WEIGHT` when pinned. In `compose_rank`, pinned adds exactly `PINNED_WEIGHT`.
- A net-zero outcome record (correct equal to incorrect) scores the same as no outcome data.
mcm-engine-30-spec: - In `find_near_duplicates`, an item whose `shannon_entropy` is below `min_entropy` (`MIN_ENTROPY` = 1.5) is left out of clustering entirely: it never joins any cluster, even with an item whose normalized text is identical.
mcm-engine-32-spec:
- find_conflicts takes (id, topic_text, body_text) tuples and returns a sorted list of bare (id_a, id_b) pairs with id_a < id_b, no scores.
- A pair is a candidate when topic similarity >= topic_threshold and body similarity <= body_threshold, using the module's MinHash signature similarity. TOPIC_THRESHOLD = 0.5 and BODY_THRESHOLD = 0.4 are new constants in mcm_engine.dedup. Rows with an empty body, or a topic below min_entropy, are skipped.
- For a rule, topic_text is its title plus keywords and body_text is its content; only active rules (not archived, not superseded) are compared.
- add_rule never supersedes. When the new rule conflicts with an existing active rule, its reply gains a note containing the word "conflict" and the text "supersede_rule"; otherwise the reply must not contain the word "conflict".
- find_conflicting_rules is read-only and writes both ids of each pair as "#<id>".

sohot-438-spec:
- shard_sets(siblings) maps each complete split variant (keyed by its filename stem before -NNNNN-of-MMMMM.gguf) to the sum of its part sizes. A set counts only when all M of its parts are listed with a nonzero size; an incomplete set is no variant and adds nothing to smallest(). mmproj and imatrix files are never parts.
- smallest() returns the bytes of the cheapest variant, single file or complete split set, or 0.
- A single servable file is a stray, ignored by both smallest() and choose(), only when it is under 1/16 of the smallest complete split set; a single quant about a quarter the size of a split set is still a variant and can be chosen.
